claims.text: ``--quick`` runs this one. It is the probe that would have caught both real incidents on day one, so if only one probe can be afforded, it is this one.
claims.why: The claim about catching real incidents references external history not present in this chunk; the name and selection are visible but the incident claim cannot be verified here.

claims.text: One (lane, probe) outcome. Carries WHICH check failed, not just that one did.
claims.why: ProbeResult has failed_check and reason fields that name the specific check and transport reason.

claims.text: Name of the failed deterministic check (``nonce_absent``, ``anchored_on_decoy``, ...). Empty when the checker was never reached.
claims.why: failed_check defaults to '' and is a plain string field; the semantics match the comment.

claims.text: Machine reason from the transport (``not_authenticated``, ``connect_failed``, ...). Empty on ``ok``/``wrong_answer``.
claims.why: reason defaults to '' and is a plain string field; the comment describes its intended content.

claims.text: Did a prompt actually reach a model? ``unavailable`` means it did not.
claims.why: asked returns self.status != 'unavailable', so only 'unavailable' yields False.

claims.text: This run's result against the trailing history for the same triple.
claims.why: Comparison fields (vendor, model, probe) plus samples, median_latency_s, delta_s, prior_pass_rate, previously_passed, regressed, slower describe a comparison against history.

claims.text: Counts that keep "could not ask" apart from "answer was wrong".
claims.why: summary returns separate 'asked' and 'could_not_ask' keys and by_status with individual statuses, keeping them distinct.

claims.text: ``asked`` and ``could_not_ask`` are separate top-level keys and ``by_status`` reports every member of the closed vocabulary individually. There is deliberately no combined "failures" number: a single number is exactly where the two get merged.
claims.why: summary returns 'asked', 'could_not_ask', and 'by_status' with all CANARY_STATUSES keys; no combined failures key is present.

claims.text: Non-zero only when a previously-passing LIVENESS probe now fails.
claims.why: exit_code returns 1 if self.regressions('liveness') is non-empty, else 0. regressions filters on c.regressed and severity, which implies previously-passing liveness probes.

claims.text: Not "something is red": a lane that has never passed is not a regression, and an unavailable lane is not a failure at all.
claims.why: regressions only counts comparisons with c.regressed True; a never-passed lane would have previously_passed False and not be marked regressed; unavailable lanes are not counted as failures in exit_code.

claims.text: One vendor endpoint plus the callable that asks it a question.
claims.why: Lane has vendor, model, endpoint, and ask fields.

claims.text: ``ask`` is ``(prompt: str, timeout_s: float) -> VendorReply``. Injecting it is what lets the whole runner be tested with fakes and no network: the tests never construct an adapter, never touch a CLI and never open a socket.
claims.why: The claim about tests never constructing adapters or opening sockets refers to test code outside this chunk; the signature of ask is visible but the testing behaviour is not.

claims.text: ``adapter`` is the seat ``ask`` was bound from, when there was one. It is carried for ONE reason: :func:`live_egress_lanes` has to hand something to :func:`session.live_egress_seats`, and a bare closure is not classifiable. Nothing in the runner reads it -- the canary still calls ``ask`` and only ``ask``, so a fake lane stays a fake lane.
claims.why: The claim about live_egress_lanes and session.live_egress_seats and the runner not reading adapter references functions and code outside this chunk; the field exists but the usage cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Resolve a vendor CLI to something ``CreateProcess`` can actually launch.
claims.why: resolve_exe uses shutil.which to find an executable path, which is what CreateProcess would need.

claims.text: On Windows a node CLI ships as an extensionless shell script beside a ``.exe``/``.cmd`` shim, and only the shim is launchable without a shell.
claims.why: The claim about Windows node CLI packaging is external knowledge not verifiable from this code chunk.

claims.text: Preferring the native ``.exe`` also skips the ``.cmd`` layer entirely -- the layer that truncated a multi-line argv and started all of this.
claims.why: The historical incident about argv truncation is external context; the code does prefer .exe first but the incident claim is not verifiable here.

claims.text: (The prompt still goes on stdin regardless; the arrival probe is what proves that end to end rather than asserting it.)
claims.why: The claim about prompt going on stdin and the arrival probe proving it refers to adapter behaviour and probe implementation outside this chunk.

claims.text: Returns ``name`` unchanged when nothing is found, so the spawn fails as ``not_on_path`` -> ``unavailable`` instead of guessing.
claims.why: The function returns name unchanged after the for loop if no candidate is found.

claims.text: Two overrides every canary adapter needs, and nothing else.
claims.why: The mixin defines exactly two methods: assemble and argv.

claims.text: The council's data-notice preamble is for model-written evidence. A canary prompt is generated in this file and carries none -- and the preamble would sit AHEAD of the arrival nonce, destroying the head position that probe measures. So the probe body goes out verbatim.
claims.why: The claim about the council's preamble and the arrival nonce head position refers to behaviour outside this chunk; the override returns the prompt unchanged, but the rationale cannot be verified here.

observations.what: probes_for with quick=True will raise KeyError if QUICK_PROBE is not in PROBES, but QUICK_PROBE is statically defined as 'arrival' and PROBES contains an arrival ProbeSpec, so it cannot fail.
ProbeResult.to_record truncates reply to REPLY_TRIM without indicating truncation; a consumer could misinterpret a truncated reply as complete.

CanaryRun.summary counts liveness_failures and quality_failures using FAILING_STATUSES but the exact membership of FAILING_STATUSES is not defined in this chunk, so the semantics of 'failure' are not pinned here.

_CanaryOllama.argv returns [] unconditionally, bypassing the resolve_exe logic that other adapters use; this is intentional per the pragma comment but means any CLI-based Ollama invocation would be impossible.

resolve_exe checks candidates in order .exe, .cmd, .bat, name; if a .cmd exists but no .exe, it returns the .cmd path, which may still be subject to the argv truncation the docstring describes, but the docstring only claims preference, not exclusion.
_is_local_http only matches http(s) URLs; an endpoint without a scheme (e.g., 'localhost:8000') would be treated as non-local even if it is local.
